text:
Nashville comes to Los Angeles on a four-game winning streak, the latest a 3-1 win over St. Louis, and has outscored opponents 15-8 in that run. The Kings are coming off a 5-2 home loss to Pittsburgh that ended the Penguins' four-game winless run, and they're 2-3-0 in their last five without Mats Zuccarello (upper body). Artemi Panarin has taken his spot beside Erik Haula and Alex Laferriere, and Erik Gustafsson has moved onto the first power-play unit. Haula also faces his old team for the first time after 132 games with the Predators.

The teams are close on chance quality. Our model projects 2.98 expected goals (the quality of shots a team generates) for Nashville and 3.08 for Los Angeles. In net, projected starter Juuse Saros is +6.3 in goals saved above expected (how many goals a goalie has stopped beyond what the shots should have produced) this season, while Darcy Kuemper is at -5.0 and would play his 500th NHL game. Los Angeles also takes 4.1 penalties a game, which keeps handing opponents power plays. Jonathan Marchessault is day-to-day and could return for Nashville.

Among the players to watch, Panarin is 74% for a point and Adrian Kempe 38% to score. Steven Stamkos is 37% to score for the Predators, and Roman Josi, who the Predators drafted 38th overall in 2008, is one point from 800 for his career. Our under-the-radar pick is Quinton Byfield, 50% for a point against a season pace of 43%, because his line creates 4.01 expected goals per 60 minutes with him on the ice.
